samples.summary: All three new frontend presence tests pass identically before and after the change (the frontend edit is type-only), so they don't cover the bug they cite
samples.evidence: The frontend hunk changes only TypeScript annotations ({blockId, offset} -> DocPosition). At runtime recordHistoryPresence already did p.set({ activeCursorPos: cursor }) with the caller's object (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2904-2911), every call site passes consumePendingCursor() verbatim (e.g. lines 1422-1425), and clampPosToModel (lines 957-977) already spread lineAffinity through. So 'an edit does not erase the caret lineAffinity from presence', 'undo restores the caret lineAffinity that was recorded' and 'leaves a position with no affinity exactly as it was' would all be green on pre-change code. They are useful shape guards but cannot demonstrate the claimed 'erased after each edit' behavior (problem site #2 in docs/tasks/active/20260822-caret-line-affinity-todo.md:15-17).

samples.summary: The new lineAffinity-undefined fallback in resolvePositionPixel is never exercised with a position carrying a non-default affinity
samples.evidence: `const affinity = lineAffinity ?? position.lineAffinity ?? 'backward'` is the stated safety net for future call sites. No test passes undefined for the parameter together with a position carrying lineAffinity: 'forward': test/view/peer-cursor.test.ts:88/107/130 all pass an explicit 'backward', and the only undefined-parameter case in the new suite is peer('none') (caret-line-affinity.test.ts:322,339) whose position also has no affinity, so it cannot distinguish the fallback from the old hardcoded 'backward'. All production call sites (cursor.ts:73, selection.ts:268-269, editor.ts:1568, editor.ts:2821) pass explicit values.

samples.summary: scrollToPosition switching from hardcoded 'backward' to pos.lineAffinity has no test
samples.evidence: The diff changes scrollToPosition's resolve affinity (editor.ts:2819-2825), one of the two problem sites named in docs/tasks/active/20260822-caret-line-affinity-todo.md:14. Grepping scrollToPosition under packages/docs/test returns nothing — only src/, frontend/docs-view.tsx and markdown match — so the peer-jump behavior the new comment describes is unasserted.

samples.summary: The rewritten restoreLocalCursor path is not tested with a position that carries an affinity
samples.evidence: restoreLocalCursor was rewritten (editor.ts:3623-3634) to spread cursorPos and let moveTo read the affinity off it — the remote-change anchor round-trip. Every existing caller in tests passes an affinity-free position (table-link.test.ts:114,127,141,156,173; edit-link-in-place.test.ts:133,178,229,284; link-trailing-edge.test.ts:179,202) and the new caret-line-affinity.test.ts never calls it, so 'forward affinity survives the restore, clamping still applies' is covered only for the undo/redo variant of the same pattern.

samples.summary: First assertion of 'the caret position always states its reading' re-asserts the harness's own default
samples.evidence: caretAt builds {blockId, offset} with no affinity and routes it through _setSelectionForTest -> cursor.moveTo(range.focus), which defaults to 'backward'; expect(...lineAffinity).toBe('backward') therefore restates the value the helper fed in and holds for any implementation that materializes a default. The following ArrowRight -> 'forward' assertion is the load-bearing one.

mergedFrom.summary: restoreLocalCursor now spreads the resolved position's affinity, but every existing test calls it without one

finding.summary: The undo/redo presence-restore path that now carries lineAffinity has no test
finding.evidence: editor.ts undo (≈2030) and redo (≈2062) were changed from `cursor.moveTo({blockId, offset})` to `cursor.moveTo({...restoredPos, offset})` — a real behavior change (restored caret keeps its wrap-boundary reading). No test enters that branch: it is gated on `'getPresenceCursorPos' in docStore`, and grep shows `getPresenceCursorPos` exists only in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts (plus its own test) — MemDocStore, used by every docs view test including the new caret-line-affinity.test.ts, has no such method (grep in packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts: no matches). The frontend store test only covers presence bookkeeping, not the editor's cursor restore. Duplicated code in two places, so both copies are untested.

verdict.reason: A test for exactly this branch exists. packages/docs/test/view/caret-line-affinity.test.ts:80-91 defines PresenceMemDocStore, a MemDocStore subclass that implements getPresenceCursorPos()/getPresenceSelection(), which unlocks the editor's `'getPresenceCursorPos' in docStore` gate (editor.ts:2025, :2057). Three tests then drive the real editor through it: undo (:225-253), redo (:255-274) and a clamped out-of-range offset (:276-296), each asserting the rebuilt caret keeps lineAffinity 'forward' via _getCursorForTest() (editor.ts:3695, returns the live cursor.position). The assertions are non-vacuous: the caret is first parked at offset 0 with 'backward' affinity (:232-233), so a restore that rebuilt `{blockId, offset}` would yield 'backward' and fail; the clamp test also pins the spread-then-override ordering. The path is reachable because MemDocStore.snapshot() pushes an undo entry making canUndo() true (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:139-162) and EditorAPI.undo/redo are undoFn/redoFn (editor.ts:2806-2807). The reviewer's greps missed it: the presence hook lives in a test subclass, not in src/store/memory.ts.
